summary: Read-only storage analysis of the Reemtsma production org. FILE STORAGE IS ALREADY OVER THE LIMIT at 121.4% (95,850 of 78,976 MB, over by 16,874 MB) and grows ~17 GB/year. Data storage at 88.0% (66,470 of 75,520 MB). Largest single finding: the retention config for AccountHistoryTracking__c (17.1 GB, 26% of data storage, dead table with no writes since 2022-10-04) exists in DataDeletionConfig__mdt but has IsActive__c = false. Identified savings ~23.6 GB data and ~44 GB file, for ~6.4 person-days across Phases 0-2.
key_findings: File storage already 16.5 GB over the entitlement - uploads may fail, sandbox refreshes affected
AccountHistoryTracking__c retention config ReebaseAccountHistory exists with IsActive__c = false; 17.1 GB, dead table since 2022-10-04, 8.35M records past the configured 48-month retention
Images are 78% of file storage; average JPG 1.7 MB (unoptimised phone photos); 2022 cohort alone is 43.4 GB (46%)
et4ae5__IndividualEmailResult__c (+1.5 GB/yr) and Fraud_Check__c (+0.4 GB/yr) have no retention config at all
Schufa_Log__c 24-month rule is active but 2.18M records exceed 24 months - not clearing
EngagementTracking__c proves retention works: 3.55M records/yr turnover, only 76,853 older than 12 months
June 2026 assessment Phase 1 quick wins (15-18 GB) were not executed - Reebase table unchanged
org_changes_made: none - read-only audit. Only SELECT queries and the org limits API were used. No records, files, retention configurations or scheduled jobs were changed.
output: Full report at org_assessment/2026-08-12-storage-review.md: executive summary, method and reconciliation section, data storage ranked by object, per-object analysis for the top 8, file storage by type and creation year, retention gap classification against DataDeletionConfig__mdt, growth and time-to-cap for both pools, offloading options, a 4-phase action plan ranked by GB per person-day with mandatory safety rules, a parametric cost comparison, governance rules, a delta against the 2026-06-10 assessment, and 6 verification gaps.
